etymologies.etymologyHTML: First attested in 1800. From French isolation, from isolé, placed on an island (thus away from other people). Equivalent to isolate +‎ -ion.

definitions.definition: (chiefly uncountable) The state of being isolated, detached, or separated; the state of being away from other people.
(diplomacy, of a country) The state of not having diplomatic relations with other countries (either with most or all other countries, or with specified other countries).

quote.citation: 1975, W. Raymond Duncan, “Problems of Cuban Foreign Policy, chapter 20”, in Irving Louis Horowitz, editor, Cuban Communism‎[1], 5th edition, Transaction, published 1985, page 486:
quote.text: As of 1975, diplomatic ostracism is still imposed by the Organization of American States (OAS). The inter-American community also exercises a trade embargo against Cuba. But even within this context of hemispheric isolation, Havana’s diplomacy is strikingly contradictory.

quote.citation: September 1993, Jon Brook Wolfsthal, “The Israeli initiative”, in The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists‎[2], volume 49, number 7, page 8:
quote.text: Israel could offer to ease North Korea’s isolation with diplomatic recognition,  […]  ¶  […]  But Washington’s strategy of increasing North Korean isolation left no room for back-channel talks with Tel Aviv,  […]

quote.citation: 2009, Dore Gold, The Rise of Nuclear Iran: How Tehran Defies the West‎[3], Regnery Publishing, →ISBN, page 49:
quote.text: It [Europe] now pressed Washington to begin direct talks with Tehran, but Undersecretary of State Nicholas Burns, Rice’s point man on Iran, still stressed that diplomatic isolation of Iran—and not diplomatic engagement—was the only acceptable approach for dealing with the Iranian nuclear challenge.

definitions.definition: (chemistry) The obtaining of an element from one of its compounds, or of a compound from a mixture
(medicine) The separation of a patient, suffering from a contagious disease, from contact with others (compare: quarantine)
(databases) A database property that determines when and how changes made in one transaction are visible to other concurrent transactions.
(psychology) A Freudian defense mechanism in which a person suppresses a harmful thought from developing into a train of thought.
